name: block
description: Semantic container (div by default, swappable element) — the structural counterpart to Text (p).
designIntent: Layout wrappers should still mean something: section, article, figure. Block is a typed, discoverable div that picks the element matching the content's role, with an inline (span) variation for flow contexts — no default decoration, so it composes with any utilities.

props.name: inline
props.description: Shorthand for as="span" — inline flow instead of a block box.

props.name: muted
props.description: Use the muted-foreground token for the block's text.

examples.title: Semantic containers
examples.code:
<Block as="section" className="space-y-2">
  <Heading level={3}>Related</Heading>
  <Text size="sm" muted>Prose lives in Text, not Block.</Text>
</Block>

<Block as="figure">…</Block>

{/* Inline flow */}
<Block inline>…</Block>

antiPatterns.title: Don't put paragraphs inside Block
antiPatterns.explanation: Copy belongs in Text (p). Block is structure — mixing them loses document semantics.

antiPatterns.title: Don't default to div when a landmark fits
antiPatterns.explanation: If the content is a section of page structure, as="section"/"article" gives assistive tech navigable landmarks for free.

accessibility.implementation: as/inline map to real intrinsic elements (semantic by selection)
accessibility.userRequirements: Pick the element that matches the content role

accessibility.implementation: Block renders no focusable content of its own
accessibility.userRequirements: Interactive children carry their own keyboard/ARIA behavior

compositionRules.relationship: Block wraps structure; Text and Heading provide the content semantics
Compose layout as Block → Flex/Grid → Text/Heading hierarchies
